title: GS Retail signs MOU with veterans ministry to expand social contribution programs - 헤럴드경제
content: GS Retail announced Friday it has signed an MOU with the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs to expand social contribution activities aimed at honoring and supporting national merit holders. The agreement, titled the "Patriots and Veterans Social Contribution MOU," was signed Thursday at the Memorial Hall of the Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea in Seodaemun-gu, Seoul, with Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs Minister Kwon O-eul and GS Retail CEO Heo Seo-hong in attendance. The MOU builds on a decade of "love for the nation" initiatives GS Retail has carried out since launching a Dokdo awareness campaign in 2017, formalizing those efforts into an ongoing social contribution program. The company has also designated veterans support as one of its core social contribution themes this year. Under the agreement, GS Retail and the ministry plan to pursue three initiatives: practical support for national merit holders and their families, activities to raise awareness of the contributions of independence movement figures, and employee volunteer programs. As a first step, GS Retail will support the installation of smart information boards as part of the ministry's "Seeing Independence Merit Holders Clearly" project. The boards provide the public with information on the lives and achievements of lesser-known independence movement contributors. The Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs has installed smart information boards at more than 50 gravesites of independence merit holders since August. GS Retail plans to fund the installation of boards at 18 additional gravesites located outside national cemeteries. The company will also provide daily necessities and food to national merit holders and their families, and will work with the Independence Hall of Korea to give children from immigrant backgrounds opportunities to learn about and experience the history of the independence movement. GS Retail will also formalize regular volunteer activities for its employees. The company plans to use its nationwide stores — including GS25 and GS The Fresh locations — as well as its mobile app to continue raising awareness of veterans commemorations and the contributions of independence movement figures.

Geopolitical competition, active conflict, technological innovation, and a widening definition of national security are driving a supercycle of investment. title: GS Group Hackathon: 900+ Solve Field Challenges with AI - 조선일보
content: Generative AI solutions developed for real-world operational issues at 5th annual event GS Group has positioned artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technologies alongside eco-friendliness as the twin pillars of its future innovation strategy, accelerating AI transformation centered on field operations. The plan involves integrating AI technology into traditional core businesses to restructure competitive advantages. GS Group holds an annual Silicon Valley-style idea competition, the "GS Group Hackathon," to spread a culture of AI innovation across the group. Employees from all affiliates participate, developing solutions that apply AI to solve real-world challenges on-site. ◇900+ People Gather to Solve Field Challenges with AI The 5th GS Group Hackathon, held in September at the Westin Seoul Parnas in Gangnam-gu, Seoul, focused on the theme "‘Play with GenAI’ Season 3: Build & Act." This emphasized creating functional AI-driven results for immediate application in work and business operations, rather than merely proposing ideas. The event drew 923 participants, including 797 GS affiliates employees and 126 external participants. Over 1.5 days, participants defined problems, derived solutions, and built initial generative AI-based services. They tackled tasks using "AI-ready data"—refined datasets that AI can instantly learn and analyze. Raw data from business sites like power plants and convenience stores often lack standardized formats, making processing time-consuming. To address this bottleneck, GS has systematically refined data accumulated across its diverse operations. The internal innovation team "52g" has organized tacit knowledge, such as the expertise of skilled workers at GS Donghae Power, into AI-readable formats. They are also developing a "power plant-specific model" that understands on-site workflows. GS plans to leverage this foundation to create industry-tailored AI solutions. The GS Group Hackathon has evolved with technological and operational changes. Launched in 2022 as a digital problem-solving event, it began integrating generative AI in 2024 and opened to external companies in 2025. Cumulative participation since its inception reaches 2,732 people. ◇GS Caltex Optimizes Processes with In-House AI Development Affiliates are also driving AI-driven innovation. GS Caltex is advancing operational transformation through "Digital & AI Transformation (DAX)," which integrates digital and AI transitions. At its Yeosu plant, the company developed in-house AI models to optimize production processes using vast operational data. Previously reliant on workers’ expertise to address process anomalies, the AI now detects early signs of issues and provides real-time solutions. GS Engineering & Construction fosters a culture of free AI use among employees. It became the first domestic construction company to adopt OpenAI’s enterprise AI solution, "ChatGPT Enterprise." Additionally, the company holds an "AI Recipe" competition to enhance employees’ AI proficiency. GS Retail promotes field-centric AI transformation. It established a system to analyze customer feedback (VOC) from convenience stores, home shopping, and supermarkets using generative AI, identifying improvement tasks. The company also formed "AX Cells" to empower field staff with generative AI tools for projects like redesigning the "Franchisee Information Sharing System," which provides tailored data to convenience store owners. Training, workshops, and AI platforms are provided to support this initiative.

title: GS Caltex Honors Citizens Who Subdued Knife Attacker in Incheon - Seoul Economic Daily
content: Citizens who subdued a knife-wielding assailant in Incheon with their bare hands have received the Cham Saram (True Person) Award from the GS Caltex Foundation. The foundation said on the 29th that it held the 2026 GS Caltex Cham Saram Award ceremony on the 28th at GS Tower in Seoul's Gangnam District. This year's recipients totaled 12, including eight people recognized for saving the lives of others, three individuals honored for acts of service to their neighbors and one organization. In the life-saving category, five citizens — Na Hyun-jun, Shin In-soo, Shin Joong-hyun, Lee Hyun-min and Kim Joong-yeon — were honored for subduing a knife-wielding assailant at a commercial building in Guwol-dong, Namdong District, Incheon, on the 13th, preventing further casualties. Also selected were Staff Sgt. Ko Young-woo of the Army 22nd Infantry Division's Geumgangsan Brigade, who rescued a child from drowning at a beach in Goseong County, Gangwon State, in July; Lee Dong-gyu, an employee of the Jeonju Facilities Management Corporation, who rescued a father and daughter at Hamdeok Beach in Jeju Special Self-Governing Province in September; and Kim Se-woong, who was stabbed while chasing a robber in Gwangju, Jeollanam-do, in February but helped police make the arrest. In the good-deeds category, awards went to Park Yoon-kyu, a dentist who has provided free treatment in medically underserved areas at home and abroad for nearly 30 years after losing a leg in an accident, and Lee Bok-dan, who has volunteered for more than 20 years delivering boxed meals and side dishes. Also honored were conductor Lee Won-sook, who has supported the independence of young people with disabilities and from low-income families through an orchestra integrating performers with and without disabilities, and Nanum Nuri Hoe, a residents' volunteer group in Gayang-dong, Gangseo District, Seoul. A GS Caltex Foundation official said, "We will continue to identify and support these devoted individuals, contributing to the realization of a just and warm society." Established in 2020, the GS Caltex Cham Saram Award is given to citizens who have devoted themselves to the lives and safety of others or performed good deeds for their neighbors. title: Kim Young-rae Promoted to Head Coach Ahead of V-League - 조선일보
content: Former acting coach secured permanent role after off-season reorganization and KOVO Cup performance [Sports Chosun Han Dong-hoon Reporter] Korea Expressway Corporation’s women’s professional volleyball acting coach Kim Young-rae has been promoted to official head coach. The team officially announced on the 29th, “We have finalized the appointment of acting coach Kim Young-rae as the official head coach in line with the V-League opening.” The 2026–2027 V-League season will commence on the 31st. Coach Kim took over as acting coach during last season’s championship finals. Although Korea Expressway Corporation finished first in the regular league, the team dismissed then-head coach Kim Jong-min. Kim, who was the head coach at the time, took charge. Korea Expressway Corporation suffered three consecutive losses to GS Caltex in the championship finals and had to settle for second place. Coach Kim successfully managed the team during the off-season. At the KOVO Cup held earlier this month, the team advanced to the finals with three consecutive wins but lost 2–3 to GS Caltex in a fierce five-set battle. Korea Expressway Corporation explained, “Coach Kim Young-rae demonstrated meticulous and sophisticated game management skills, reading the overall flow of the match and effectively guiding the players on the court, as befits a leader with a background as a setter. The club highly evaluated his leadership in swiftly reorganizing and strengthening the team during the off-season, leading to the confirmation of his appointment as official head coach.” Coach Kim stated, “I sincerely thank the club for believing in me and giving me this opportunity, as well as the citizens of Gimcheon and fans for their unwavering support. I will do my best to balance the team and, based on our strengthened roster, aim to reach the top of the V-League this season.” Korea Expressway Corporation declared, “Following last season’s regular league championship and this year’s KOVO Cup runner-up finish, we have once again proven our status as a top-tier team in the league. With successful reinforcement through this year’s rookie draft, we will challenge for the championship with an even more solid lineup.”

title: GS Caltex Kicks Off New Season with Home Opener, Sparki Debut - 조선일보
content: Team unveils AI cheer song, championship ceremony, and interactive fan events at Jangchung Gymnasium [OSEN=Cho Eun-hye Reporter] The GS Caltex Seoul Kixx volleyball team opens the new season against Korea Expressway Corporation. Led by head coach Lee Young-taek, GS Caltex will hold the home opener of the HK Insurance 2026-2027 V-League at Jangchung Gymnasium in Seoul on the 31st. GS Caltex plans to sing the cheer songs created by fans together on-site, adding to the heated atmosphere of the home opener. Inside Jangchung Gymnasium, a cabinet-style photo zone has been set up, allowing fans to freely change props, stickers, magnets, and other items inside the cabinets to take their own special commemorative photos. Georgia Southern University researchers can now compete for federal funding, including Department of Defense funding that requires strict cybersecurity protections, after the university’s Talon Secure virtual environment earned Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Level 2 certification. With Talon Secure certified, Georgia Southern faculty can pursue larger grants, support current Department of Defense-funded projects and join defense companies as research partners or subcontractors. Inside Talon Secure, researchers can store and work with government information that is unclassified but still must be safeguarded, such as technical data tied to defense programs. The certification confirms the system meets federal requirements for protecting that information. “Protecting sensitive research isn’t a box we check, it’s a standard we hold ourselves to every day,” said Georgia Southern Vice President for Research and Innovation David Weindorf, Ph.D. “This certification opens the door for our faculty to compete for consequential defense research, and it tells our federal partners they can bring that work to Georgia Southern with confidence.” Talon Secure was reviewed by a Certified Third-Party Assessor Organization and earned a perfect score, with no deficiencies in any of the 14 security categories tested. Several Georgia Southern departments collaborated to prepare for the audit, including the Office of Research Integrity, Research Security and Export Controls and Information Technology Services. Janny Crespo-Grow, Ph.D., director of the Office of Research Integrity, said the assessor described Georgia Southern’s performance as “the standard for what we should see in our assessments.” Crespo-Grow, part of the Office of Research Integrity, specifically credited Chief Information Security Officer Nic Carroll and his team, who “took point” in preparation. Carroll highlighted the cross-divisional collaboration behind the audit. “Preparing for the audit meant bringing together people from the Office of Research and Innovation, IT, information security and compliance to answer one honest question: ‘Does what we actually do every day match what our written procedures say we do?’” he said. He added assessors tested 110 security controls against 320 assessment objectives. “The assessment confirmed our protections are followed in practice, not just written down, and that is what gives our researchers an environment they can trust,” Carroll said.

title: Benny G’s Mom, a Breast Cancer Survivor, Emotionally Introduces Him to the Grand Ole Opry Stage on Opry Goes Pink Night - American Songwriter
content: Benny G got a very special introduction to the Grand Ole Opry stage. The singer performed during Opry Goes pink, an annual concert put on in partnership with Susan G. Komen amid Breast Cancer Awareness month. Ahead of Benny’s performance, Opry host Kelly Sutton stepped aside to allow the singer’s mom, breast cancer survivor Ali Goldsmith, to introduce her son. “Five years ago I was diagnosed at the age of 43 with metastatic breast cancer,” Goldsmith began. She went on to shout out the doctors who cared for her amid her illness, before turning the focus to her son. “I believe that every single soul is an entire universe,” she said. “So naturally, there is no greater blessing in my life than the three incredible lights that I refer to as my children.” Goldsmith went to reveal how Benny comforted her during the height of her illness. “When I was ill, he would sit at the edge of my bed with his acoustic guitar and we would sing songs together by many of the artists that performed on this legendary stage,” she said. “It was music and my unwavering faith that gave me both comfort and strength during such a challenging time.” “I want to thank the Grand Ole Opry for shining a bright pink light on this awful disease and also giving me the honor of introducing this next performer,” Goldsmith continued. “This truly is our full circle moment. So with all the joy in my heart, which I refer to is nachas, ladies and gentlemen, let’s give a Grand Ole Opry welcome to my son, Benny G.” “Love you mom, first of all,” he said. “This first song I’m going to play you guys is actually inspired by my mom and her perseverance and faith when she had cancer… It’s called ‘Heaven Knows We Just Keep Dancing Through It All,’ ’cause that’s what life’s about, really.” Next, Benny performed “In the Now,” a song he co-wrote with his sister, Ella Goldsmith. The 19-year-old performer concluded his set by welcoming Briley King back out onto the stage. The pair performed a cover of Marvin Gaye and Tammi Terrell’s “Ain’t No Mountain High Enough.” Benny wasn’t the only star on hand for the special Opry show. Deana Carter opened up the night, and was followed by sets from Mackenzie Carpenter and Megan Moroney. Additionally, Jillian Cardarelli made her Grand Ole Opry debut. Audience members were also treated to solo sets by both King and Mandy Barnett.

title: Freddy Carrick-Smith’s 12th in Sölden Makes British GS History - Ski Racing Media
content: Freddy Carrick-Smith scored his first World Cup points in Sölden, finishing 12th in the 2026/27 men’s season-opening giant slalom. Lucas Pinheiro Braathen won the race with his fourth straight elite giant slalom victory. Carrick-Smith’s result gave Britain its first men’s World Cup GS top 30 since March 2022. Carrick-Smith’s twin brother Zak and elder brother Luca watched from the finish area. His mother, four-time British Olympian Emma Carrick-Anderson, remains his technician and watched from the wings. Freddy’s father, Phil Smith, remains watched from the top. Freddy heard him last before pushing out of the Rettenbach start gate. This wasn’t just Freddy’s first World Cup points result. It also put Britain back on the giant slalom map. His family has worked nearly 20 years for this moment. Speaking exclusively with the Skiing Is Believing podcast less than 24 hours after the race, Carrick-Smith said, “The whole family was there … and we were over the moon after the second run.” This was only Carrick-Smith’s fifth World Cup start and second in Sölden. He made his World Cup debut there 12 months earlier. He finished 54th after the first run, more than 1.6 seconds outside the top 30. Carrick-Smith started with bib 46 and tied Norway’s Hans Grahl-Madsen for 21st after Run 1. “When I saw the 21st on the screen, I was happy and actually snapped my pole while celebrating,” he said. He then produced the fifth-fastest second run and climbed nine places. The course had one speed trap before the final flat, measuring the speed racers carried into the closing stretch. Carrick-Smith posted the fastest reading in Run 1 at 82.20 km/h. His 80.20 km/h in Run 2 ranked second. Carrick-Smith summed up what the result meant to him: “If you don’t enjoy the journey, you’re not going to enjoy the result.” Jeremy Palmer-Tomkinson’s ninth-place finish in Méribel, France, on March 10, 1968, remains Britain’s best men’s World Cup GS result. Carrick-Smith’s 12th was the country’s best in the discipline since then. Charlie Raposo had Britain’s last men’s World Cup GS top 30 before Sölden. He finished 27th in Kranjska Gora on March 12, 2022, then placed 16th the next day. Raposo was in Sölden on Sunday and told Ski Racing Media, “I’m very glad that someone has come along and taken that.” Raposo also praised Carrick-Smith’s skiing and focus between runs: “It was super fun to watch. He was calm, super dialed and super focused between runs so super excited for him.” Carrick-Smith also became the first British man to score World Cup points in Sölden. Chemmy Alcott remains Britain’s top finisher there, placing 10th in 2008. This result means the Carrick-Smith family’s schedule for late November and December now looks a little different. Freddy’s 12th-place finish opened a start opportunity for Zak at the men’s World Cup giant slalom in Copper Mountain, Colorado, on Nov. 29. Before then, Freddy might make his World Cup slalom debut in Levi, Finland, on Nov. 15. Dave Ryding’s retirement after the 2026 Olympic Winter Games could create an opening alongside slalom specialists Laurie Taylor and Billy Major. Freddy and Zak turn 20 in February. The Sölden result gives Freddy a chance, with limited pressure, to leave his footprint in the snow. It could also put two Carrick-Smith brothers on a World Cup start list together. The next generation of British athletes is stepping up to the top level. Whether it’s Freddy, Luca or Zak, the Carrick-Smith name on the World Cup results sheet is one fans may have to get used to. The Skiing Is Believing podcast also featured Carrick-Smith in its Sölden review show. Listen below on Spotify or YouTube, with special guests Britt Janyk and William St-Germain. title: Funding the Next Infrastructure Cycle: The Evolving Financing Playbook - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Goldman Sachs’ weekly newsletter, offering economic and markets analysis from across the firm. Subscribe now. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. While the AI buildout is inherently a technology race, the scale of investment now underway suggests it is equally a capital formation challenge. Scaling AI requires investment in a much wider buildout of physical infrastructure, creating capital needs across data centers, power, networks, construction, equipment, and more. The magnitude of the buildout has also risen sharply. Just a year ago, estimates for AI infrastructure investment over a five-year period lay between $3 trillion and $5 trillion. Earlier this year, the Goldman Sachs Global Institute approximated that number could reach $8 trillion over the next four to five,1 while other sources have more recently estimated it could swell past $10 trillion.2 That investment is not likely to be a one-time deployment, as a substantial share of AI spending is directed toward equipment inside data centers that requires more frequent replacement. “This is not a one-time $10 trillion investment,” says Mahesh Saireddy, global co-head of the Capital Solutions Group within Global Banking & Markets. “Technology will continue to evolve, driving recurring investment cycles for years to come.” The direct beneficiaries of the AI buildout are well known: hyperscalers, chipmakers, data center operators. But the investment cycle is creating demand throughout a broader ecosystem of businesses and assets. “It is creating an entire second generation of the AI economy,” Saireddy says, pointing to cloud providers, data center construction companies, and power-related businesses. Goldman Sachs Research expects global data center power demand to increase by 170% between 2025 and 2030, with more than 60% of that growth coming from the United States.3 Yet the infrastructure opportunity remains a global one, with investment activity accelerating in Europe and Asia as well. Still, AI is not the sole driver of capital markets activity. The broader story includes continued growth in alternatives assets, renewed M&A financing needs, and a global infrastructure buildout extending beyond AI alone. Alternative asset managers, historically invested predominantly in private equity, are growing larger and more complex, demanding a broader set of financing solutions across private credit, infrastructure, insurance capital, derivatives, and long-duration investment strategies. “Now everyone has become large, diversified alts,” Saireddy notes, adding that as those businesses grow, so does the need for tailored financing across different asset classes. That expansion is taking place against a more challenging backdrop for traditional private equity. Saireddy notes that average disposition times have risen to more than seven years, leaving many sponsors with older assets to manage while exit activity remains subdued. While he expects some of those assets to clear over the next year or two, he remains constructive on private equity’s longer-term role, especially given the scale of the global equity market. Private credit is a particularly important part of that evolution, but it is no longer synonymous only with direct lending. Private investment-grade lending makes up the second phase of private credit’s development, supported in part by alternative managers’ insurance platforms and separately managed accounts. Saireddy says that for long-duration assets such as data centers and related infrastructure, private investment-grade capital can especially be a natural fit: “Data centers have a lot of duration too, which is a great asset to go into the insurance platforms.” Going forward, private capital will play an increasingly complementary role alongside the public markets, as the AI buildout calls for greater coordination across capital sources. The right financing mix will depend on an asset’s size, duration, risk profile, and where it sits in the development cycle. Companies with substantial financial capacity are driving the AI investment cycle, with Saireddy noting that the largest hyperscalers remain relatively low-levered and with “massively positive free cash flow,” providing a strong foundation for continued investment. But funding the next AI growth phase will not be linear. Assumptions around AI monetization and the viability of the broader buildout will continue to evolve, as will credit spreads and valuations. “There will be market corrections,” Saireddy cautions. Ultimately, Saireddy believes that the supercycle will get financed. But spreads may fluctuate with supply, and equity investors are likely to remain especially discerning. The IPO market remains open, but investor demand is concentrated in growth-oriented and AI-linked businesses rather than spread evenly across sector and issuer type. Capital coordination will emerge as a defining feature of this technology supercycle. For companies and investors that can align the right capital with the right assets, match financing duration to infrastructure life cycles, and thoughtfully combine public and private solutions, the opportunity is substantial. 1 Harnessing AI for the Real Economy, Goldman Sachs Investment Banking (2026) 2 Financing the AI Buildout, The Brookings Institution (2026) 3 Navigating a System of AI Bottlenecks, Goldman Sachs Investment Banking (2026)

title: 2027 Triumph Tiger 1200 Aims For The BMW GS's Do-Everything Crown - Jalopnik
content: If you want a motorcycle that does everything, you buy a BMW GS. It's such an easy choice, so rote that even BMW itself has felt the need to specialize its adventure lineup away from such perfectly omnicapable bikes. Now, though, another brand thinks it can hit the Bavarians where their hold is strongest. Triumph has revamped the Tiger 1200 lineup to hit BMW where it hurts, and the Brits have a solid shot of making a real mark. The Tiger 1200 line is still split into its four component models — GT Pro, Rally Pro, GT Explorer, and Rally Explorer — but Triumph has streamlined things between the four bikes to make their differences clearer. Every model now comes with a 19 inch front wheel and a 17 out back, and all four get trick self-lowering Showa suspension with 7.9 inches of travel front and rear — until you come to a stop, at which point the system drops the bike almost 1.2 inches. Triumph says the seat height, with a low seat installed and the self-lowering suspension active, can get as low as 31.1 inches at a stop. That's impressively low for a big adventure bike, and over an inch shorter than the competing R 1300 GS. On top of the trick suspension updates, Triumph has updated the Tiger's rider display — a new 7-inch display with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto now standard. There's also the updated 1,160cc three-cylinder engine with a redesigned cylinder head, new pistons, lighter intake and exhaust valves, and revised gear ratios for first, second, and third. The engine now makes 155.8 horsepower (up from 147 hp). Triumph also claims that the new Tiger 1200 has more torque down low, which improves slow-speed performance. If you're a bit confused by all the Tiger 1200's available variants, here's how Triumph differentiates them: GT bikes get cast wheels, while the Rally bikes get spokes. Rally bikes get an extra off-road ride mode and some engine protection. Explorer bikes get wider and taller handlebars and 7.9-gallon fuel tanks rather than the Pro bikes' 5.3-gallon units. Got all that? Essentially, they're the same chassis, engine, and suspension across all models, but the Rally bikes get some dirt features, and Explorer bikes get the right gear for long tours. All four get Bosch radar front and rear, as well, to enable both adaptive cruise control and rear close-follow warnings — they're all competent tourers, big tank or no. The best change for 2027 to my eye, though, is the appearance of the new Tiger 1200 lineup. The prior bikes were stuck in an awkward in-between period, where Triumph was in the process of ditching its long-lasting twin-headlight design but hadn't yet gone all-in on compact LED illumination. Now it has, and the Tiger looks all the better for it — that single center headlight below the light bar really works for me. It's functional, too, with corner lighting built into the central LED that illuminates when the rider leans.

title: GS Entec's Ulsan Plant: Asia's Largest Offshore Wind Hub - 조선일보
content: 300 Billion Won Facility Automates Monopile Production for 15MW Turbines, Secures Major Contracts GS Group is accelerating its expansion into the eco-friendly energy ecosystem. The company has transformed GS Entec, which previously manufactured large-scale equipment for GS Caltex and other petrochemical plants, into Asia’s largest production hub for offshore wind turbine foundations. GS Entec held a completion ceremony on October 26 at its Ulsan Yongjam Plant for a 300 billion Korean won automated production facility dedicated to monopiles. Monopiles are massive steel pillars driven into the seabed to support offshore wind turbines. The event was attended by GS Group Chairman Huh Tae-soo, GS Co., Ltd. Vice Chairman Hong Soon-ki, GS Entec CEO Huh Chul-hong, and Koen Bogers, CEO of Dutch partner Sif. Chairman Huh has shown particular interest in the business transition, reportedly visiting the site multiple times to monitor progress. GS Entec has long produced ultra-large chemical equipment, including pressure vessels and heat exchangers for petrochemical plants. However, as global carbon neutrality efforts slowed traditional petrochemical plant orders, the company had to revise its survival strategy. GS Group and GS Entec found a solution in technological continuity: the precision machining and welding of thick steel plates required for petrochemical pressure vessels closely resemble the processes needed for monopile production. Partnering with Sif, the world’s top monopile manufacturer, GS Entec began overhauling its Ulsan factory in October 2024, automating key processes. With an annual production capacity of 150,000 tons, the facility is Asia’s first and largest capable of producing monopiles for 15MW-class offshore wind turbines. It has already secured contracts to supply 64 monopiles worth 200 billion Korean won for the Yeonggwang Nakwol Offshore Wind Project (365MW) and 37 large monopiles for the Taean Offshore Wind Project. Leveraging this track record, GS Entec plans to aggressively target markets in Japan and other parts of Asia.
